scenarios.title: Restore independent uplinks in a two-tier campus
scenarios.summary: Restore independent campus uplinks and prove the stated structural outage paths.
scenarios.objective: Connect each access device to two different combined distribution/core devices. Two cables to the same device are not two independent uplinks. Complete every supplied cable; use each physical port at most once and keep the two protected cables unchanged. Keep a hierarchy path between North access and South access with all devices available, with West combined unavailable, and with East combined unavailable.
hints: Compare each cable’s device role and building, not just whether it has two ends.
Count different upstream devices. A second cable to the same device shares that device’s failure.
Check every stated case; the first working normal path is not the whole task.
scenarios.simplifications: Source check 2026-11-13: current CCNA v1.1 objectives 1.2a/b and Cisco Campus LAN/WLAN design guide (2020). Bounded structural routed-adjacency model only: no packets, IP configuration, STP, convergence, bandwidth, routing policy or actual hardware. Building-local access and non-transit access roles are explicit exercise requirements, not universal claims for every campus. Other architecture subtopics remain separate.
scenarios.explanation: The access switches need independent connections to both combined devices. A normal path through West alone can work while the design still fails when West is lost. Count distinct parent devices, not cables. The cable identities are fixed, but any compatible unused ports that satisfy every role and failure check are accepted.

scenarios.title: Repair building and core paths in a three-tier campus
scenarios.summary: Repair a three-tier campus’s building links and redundant core paths.
scenarios.objective: Connect each access device only to distribution devices in its own named building. Keep two different upstream devices for every access and distribution device. Complete all supplied cables without sharing a physical port. Edit only a-dn1, a-ds1, w-dn2 and e-ds2; preserve the other cable endpoints. Keep a hierarchy path from North access to South access with all devices available and after each stated single core or distribution device outage.
hints: Compare each cable’s device role and building, not just whether it has two ends.
Count different upstream devices. A second cable to the same device shares that device’s failure.
Check every stated case; the first working normal path is not the whole task.
scenarios.simplifications: Source check 2026-11-13: current CCNA v1.1 objectives 1.2a/b and Cisco Campus LAN/WLAN design guide (2020). Bounded structural routed-adjacency model only: no packets, IP configuration, STP, convergence, bandwidth, routing policy or actual hardware. Building-local access and non-transit access roles are explicit exercise requirements, not universal claims for every campus. Other architecture subtopics remain separate.
scenarios.explanation: A three-tier path crosses access, the local distribution block, the core, the remote distribution block and the remote access device. A cable to the wrong building can be physically connected and still violate that organization. Fix local access links and missing core uplinks, then test each stated outage; a working normal path is only part of the assignment.
